clues.title: Plate: black with two white sections
text: Malaysian licence plates are **black** and generally have **two** white sections. These are visible even when blurred.
NOTE: Indonesian licence plates can also be black, but they will have **three** white sections.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Black plates with two white sections, still visible when blurred. Indonesian plates can be black too but have three white sections.

differs.how: Indonesian black plates have three white sections

clues.title: Road lines: double white centre line
text: Malaysia frequently uses **double white** centre lines on its two-lane roads. It is the only Southeast Asian country to do so.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Double white centre lines on two-lane roads. The only Southeast Asian country that does this.

clues.title: Road: thick yellow bars
text: These **thick yellow bars** are also almost exclusive to Malaysia.
NOTE: You can very rarely see similar patterns in [Hong Kong](https://maps.app.goo.gl/PSUAhJVM8bCQUhH36) and the [United Kingdom](https://maps.app.goo.gl/BKn4346rfTwJj3L26).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Thick yellow bars that are almost exclusive here. Very rarely seen in Hong Kong and the UK.

clues.title: Pole: black or white sticker
text: Electricity poles in Malaysia often have **black** or **white** stickers on them.
Sometimes you will also find red-and-white or red-and-blue stripes below the black sticker.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Electricity poles often have black or white stickers, sometimes with red-and-white or red-and-blue stripes below the black one.

clues.title: Sign: stop says BERHENTI, yield BERI LALUAN
text: **BERHENTI** stop signs and **BERI LALUAN** yield signs are both unique to Malaysia.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Stop signs say BERHENTI and yield signs say BERI LALUAN. Both are unique here.

clues.title: Bollard: black, white, grey and red
text: Malaysian bollards will often have the colours **black**, **white**, **grey** and **red**. Here are three examples of typical Malaysian bollards.
NOTE: There can be multiple varieties of these bollards, but the layout is mostly the same.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Bollards usually use black, white, grey and red. Several varieties exist but the layout is mostly the same.

clues.title: Direction sign: yellow hexagon road shield
text: This is a typical Malaysian directional sign. **Hexagonal yellow **highway shields** **are unique to Malaysia.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A typical direction sign with a yellow hexagonal highway shield. The hexagon shield is unique here.

clues.title: Kilometre marker: white and blue
text: Malaysian kilometre markers have a unique **white-and-blue **colour scheme. Note that the hexagon shields are often visible.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Kilometre markers are white and blue, and the hexagon shield is often visible. Unique colour scheme.

clues.title: Language: Malay in Latin script
text: The **Malay language** uses the Latin script. It is very closely related to Indonesian. These two languages are practically indistinguishable for people who do not speak either.

images.caption: Malay text sample in Latin script

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Malay uses Latin letters and is very close to Indonesian. They are practically indistinguishable unless you speak one.

clues.title: Language: Chinese characters on signs
text: In contrast to neighbouring Indonesia, **Chinese characters** are often seen in Malaysia. In fact, 24.6% of the Malaysian population is of Chinese descent.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Chinese characters are often seen on signs because about a quarter of the population is of Chinese descent. Indonesia has far fewer.

clues.title: Direction sign: black-and-white striped post
text: Signposts in Malaysia almost always have **black-and-white** **stripes**.
NOTE: Within Asia, these posts are also found in Sri Lanka, Bhutan, India, Nepal and Bangladesh. Make sure to check other clues before guessing.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Signposts are almost always painted with black and white stripes. Sri Lanka, Bhutan, India, Nepal and Bangladesh have them too, so check other clues.

clues.title: Kerb: black-and-white painted
text: **Black-and-white **curbs are commonly found in Malaysia.
NOTE: Many other countries in Asia can also have black-and-white curbs.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Black-and-white painted kerbs are common. Many other Asian countries have them too.

clues.title: Route marker: letter before road number
text: Each Malaysian state, excluding the three federal territories, has its own road numbering system with a **unique letter** at the start of the road number.
NOTE: Sabah also has A roads, but only the A2 and A7.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Each state, except the three federal territories, has its own road numbering with a unique starting letter. Sabah also has A roads, but only A2 and A7.

clues.title: Flags: state flags
text: **State flags** can be seen with some regularity, so it is worth learning them.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: State flags show up fairly often, so they are worth learning.

clues.title: Street sign: postal code on the sign
text: Malaysian postal codes are useful to know, since they can be found on most street signs in the country.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Postal codes appear on most street signs, and they help to place you.

clues.title: Pole: black sticker on the mainland
text: **Black pole stickers** are most commonly found on the mainland.
NOTE: The black stickers on Borneo only exist in Generation 4 coverage.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Black pole stickers are most common on the mainland. On Borneo they only exist in Gen 4 coverage.

clues.title: Pole: black sticker saying TEL TNB
text: Black stickers with the text ‘**TEL TNB**’ at the bottom, are only found in Johor.

images.caption: Zoomed circle shows the sticker on the pole reading JB 19

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Black stickers with TEL TNB at the bottom are found only in Johor, in the far south of the mainland.

clues.title: Pole: white sticker on Borneo
text: **White pole stickers** are only found on electricity poles on the island of Borneo, in Sarawak.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: White pole stickers on electricity poles only occur in Sarawak, on Borneo.

clues.title: Lamp post: two small circles on the support
text: Lamp posts with **two small circles** on the support are mainly found on mainland Malaysia.

images.caption: Red circle marks the black sticker on the utility pole under the lamp

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Lamp posts with two small circles on the support are mainly on the mainland.

clues.title: Lamp post: triangular metal support
text: Lamp posts with a **triangular metal support** are mainly found on mainland Malaysia.

images.caption: Red arrow points to the triangular metal support under the lamp

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Lamp posts with a triangular metal support are mainly on the mainland.

clues.title: Pole: 2-1 insulators, long diagonal wooden brace
text: Electricity poles on the Borneo side typically have a **2-1 insulator configuration**, and a long **diagonal wooden support**. They are exclusive to the Sarawak region of the island.
NOTE: Indonesian poles can look similar, but they are usually not made of wood, and use smaller or no diagonal supports.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: On Borneo, poles have two insulators on one side and one on the other, plus a long diagonal wooden support. Only in Sarawak. Indonesian poles look similar but are usually not wooden and have small or no diagonal supports.

differs.how: Indonesian poles are usually not wooden, with small or no brace

clues.title: Pole: thin metal with two parallel tops
text: Thin metal poles with **two parallel **pole tops are exclusive to the Sabah region of Borneo.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Thin metal poles with two parallel pole tops are only in Sabah, on Borneo.

clues.title: Lamp post: boomerang-shaped metal support
text: This lamp post with a supporting piece of sheet metal resembling a **boomerang** is found in Sarawak.
NOTE: It is more common in cities other than Kuching.

images.caption: Circle and red arrow mark the boomerang-shaped metal support on the lamp post

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A lamp post with a boomerang-shaped metal support is found in Sarawak, more often outside Kuching.

clues.title: Bin: S-shaped logo
text: Trash bins with a **logo resembling an ‘S’** are found in the states of Negeri Sembilan, Malacca and Johor.

images.caption: Circle shows the S-shaped logo on the grey bin

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Bins with an S-like logo are in Negeri Sembilan, Malacca and Johor, in the south of the mainland.

clues.title: Bin: leaf logo
text: Trash bins with a **logo resembling leaves** are found in Perlis and Kedah.

images.caption: Circle shows the leaf logo on the green-lidded bin

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Bins with a logo like leaves are in Perlis and Kedah, in the northwest of the mainland.

clues.title: Bin: sunny landscape logo, Alam Flora
text: Trash bins with this logo featuring a **sunny landscape**, saying **‘Alam Flora’** are found in Pahang, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. The logo will occasionally be absent, and it will just say ‘Alam Flora’.

images.caption: Green wheelie bin with a sunny landscape logo and Alam Flora text; the circle zooms in on the lid logo.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Bins with a sunny landscape logo and the words Alam Flora are in Pahang, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. The logo is sometimes missing, leaving just the name.

clues.title: Street sign: yellow arrow with black outline
text: **Yellow street name signs** with a black outline are specific to the state of Johor.
NOTE: This **arrow-shaped** street sign, regardless of its colour, is exclusive to Malaysia.
NOTE: Yellow signs are also found in southern [Negeri Sembilan](https://maps.app.goo.gl/HG89SePzMd5WWheo6), however only the tip of the arrow will be black.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Yellow arrow-shaped street signs with a black outline are specific to Johor. The arrow shape itself is unique here in any colour. In southern Negeri Sembilan only the tip is black.

clues.title: Street sign: green arrow, yellow JKR hexagon
text: **Green** street signs that form an arrow shape and have a **yellow hexagonal symbol **with the letters** JKR** on the left side are found in Sabah.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Green arrow-shaped street signs with a yellow hexagon marked JKR on the left are found in Sabah, on Borneo.

clues.title: Landscape: very mountainous roads on Borneo
text: Assuming you are on Borneo: the state of Sabah is **very mountainous**, and much of the coverage is on mountain roads like this one.
NOTE: Sarawak generally has flatter roads. Even if you see mountains, they will usually be at a [distance](https://goo.gl/maps/5VrnWWJCBfNgREaP7).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: If you know you are on Borneo, a very mountainous road points to Sabah. Sarawak has flatter roads, with mountains usually far away.

clues.title: Landscape: isolated rock hills in flat land
text: These **isolated rock formations**, rising abruptly from an otherwise flat landscape, can be found near the Thai border in Perlis state.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Isolated rock formations rising abruptly from flat land, near the Thai border in Perlis.

clues.title: Street: blue cylindrical containers
text: Urban areas in Labuan are dotted with **blue cylindrical containers**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Towns on Labuan island are dotted with blue cylindrical containers.

clues.title: Google car: grey car, long front antenna
text: This unique **grey car** with a long front antenna can be found in Gunung Mulu National Park, Sarawak.

images.caption: A grey car blur on a forest road with a long thin antenna at the front

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A unique grey car with a long front antenna, in Gunung Mulu National Park in Sarawak.
